title: Orion watching over ALMA
caption: Orion above ALMA antennas, ALMA Operations Support Facility, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Three dish antennas belonging to ALMA, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, stand under the Chilean night sky, with the constellation Orion, the Hunter, shining high above them. Its hourglass outline and the three bright stars of Orion's Belt make it easy to recognize. Because the photo was taken from the southern hemisphere, Orion's sword appears above the Belt.
The middle "star" of the sword is really the Orion Nebula, whose fuzzy glow can be seen without a telescope when conditions are good.

The three antennas are a small part of ALMA, which has 66 antennas in total. By combining signals from antennas spread up to 16 kilometers apart, a technique called interferometry, ALMA acts as a single giant telescope. When the photo was taken, the antennas were being tested at ALMA's Operations Support Facility, which sits lower, at 2900 meters. After testing and fitting out, the antennas were moved up to the Chajnantor plateau at 5000 meters, one of the driest places in the world.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph of ALMA antennas at night with the constellation Orion overhead. No camera settings are published.
understand.eye: A camera exposure can gather more light than the eye, so the stars may look richer than they would to someone standing beside the antennas.

explore: ALMA observes at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths, which water vapor and oxygen in Earth's atmosphere strongly absorb, so it needs a high, dry site. Early science observations began with part of the array late in 2011. Adrian Russell took the photo and shared it in the Your ESO Pictures Flickr group. ALMA is run jointly by Europe, North America and East Asia, working with the Republic of Chile.
alt: Three large dish antennas under a starry night sky, with the constellation Orion high above them.
